- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too high after sharp price spikes in history, then overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, showing a persistent lag in capturing recent downward trends.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — forecasts often remain elevated longer than actual price corrections.
- Forecasts show strong bias toward higher values, particularly when history includes recent high prices.
- Model fails to adjust for short-term volatility — overestimates during periods of high noise or rapid movement.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are systematically too high, especially in the middle to end of the forecast window.
